posts.text: 🤔 National cyber director shake-up signals Team Trump's possible concern over outages US President Donald Trump has replaced the head of the White House Office of the National Cyber Director in the aftermath of a wave of outages affecting American big tech companies, banks, airlines, and federal agencies. 🌏 Trump tapped Kirsten A. Davies, described by the White House as "a battle-tested cyber leader," to lead the office. She previously served as the Pentagon's chief information officer from December 23, 2025. 🌏 Her predecessor, Sean Cairncross, had not worked in cybersecurity before entering government. It's unclear what exactly caused Cairncross's dismissal: the inexplicable outages or his ties to former registered lobbyist and political strategist Susie Wiles, who resigned as White House chief of staff on November 5. 🌏 On November 16, Cairncross attributed widespread digital disruptions to "updating and modernizing legacy systems," adding that the Americans would see more of it. The comment was apparently unsettling, given that many in the US rushed to Costco and stocked up on bottled water amid the digital turmoil, according to The Washington Post. 🌏 Meanwhile, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin cited an unnamed tech leader who linked outages to AI. A flurry of theories has been circulating on social media for days, suggesting either rogue AI agents escaping their sandboxes again or a plot by AI tech giants to thwart open-source competitors, consolidate control over the industry, and delay a potential burst of the AI bubble. Judging by the White House's announcement, which praises Trump's cyber initiatives while taking aim at digital "enemies," the administration appears far more concerned about what could be a sudden, systemic attack than it is willing to admit. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
